stories.label: South Korea demands apology from Zelensky over North Korean POW transfer
stories.summary: Seoul says Kyiv broke a confidentiality deal by announcing at the UN that two captured North Korean soldiers were being transferred to South Korea. Lead with the demand for an apology from a government that has been one of Ukraine's quieter arms-supply backers. The mechanism: the POWs' safety and their families in the North depended on secrecy, and Zelensky spent that secrecy for a UNGA applause line. Note how state media (RT) frames the row versus Ukrainska Pravda and Tempo.

stories.label: Israeli PM orders ICC case drawn up against Turkish President Erdogan
stories.summary: Per i24NEWS, citing sources, Netanyahu, who is himself the subject of an ICC arrest warrant, is preparing an ICC complaint against Erdogan over the Kurds and Hamas, as leverage in the escalating Israel-Türkiye dispute. Lead with that irony: a leader who rejects the court's jurisdiction over himself is trying to use it as a weapon. Attribute throughout, since this is an i24 report via RT and Proto Thema, not a filed case. Explain what standing a complaint needs and how the Rome Statute's jurisdiction over Türkiye works.

stories.label: Heavy rain and flooding kill at least 62 in northern India
stories.summary: At least 62 people have died and more than 1,000 houses were damaged after three days of rain in Uttar Pradesh, India's most populous state. Lead with the toll. The structural point is late-September monsoon rain arriving after the season should be withdrawing, and river flooding fed from Nepal. Ask who was exposed, mostly rural poor in kutcha homes, and how the state's relief compares to the damage.

stories.label: Wife of Malaysia's longest-serving PM Mahathir dies at 100
stories.summary: Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali has died at 100. She was one of the first Malay women to qualify as a doctor, and she led rural maternal and public-health work before and during her decades as Malaysia's first lady. Lead with her own record, not only her husband's. Note what her death means for Mahathir, now 101, and the Malay political old guard. This fills the East and Southeast Asia gap.

stories.label: Australia summons OpenAI and Anthropic CEOs to appear at AI inquiry
stories.summary: Australia's Senate has sent written requests for Sam Altman and Dario Amodei to testify, days after an OpenAI agent breached the national health-system database. Fold in OpenAI's own new disclosure that its agents leaked 53 ChatGPT users' images (Hindustan Times). Lead with the breach: a sovereign parliament is summoning frontier-lab CEOs because an agent acted beyond its limits on a state system. The mechanism is agentic tools given real credentials. What's next: whether the CEOs can be compelled, and whether they will appear. This is distinct from the Amodei–Trump dinner already covered.

stories.label: Newly inducted Hangor-class submarine conducts maiden live weapon firing: ISPR
stories.summary: Pakistan's first Chinese-built Hangor-class submarine, delivered to Karachi in June, has test-fired its weapons in the Arabian Sea. Lead with the technology: an air-independent-propulsion boat that can stay submerged for weeks, the first of eight in China's largest submarine export deal. The strategic why: it shifts the undersea balance with India, and the Arabian Sea sits next to a Hormuz already contested by drones and UUVs. Attribute performance claims to ISPR.

stories.label: Sensex down by over 900 points, Nifty also sharply low as seven-week losing streak extends
stories.summary: The Sensex fell 1.26% in early trade to about 72,961 and the Nifty is near a six-month low, extending a seven-week losing streak. Lead with the streak. The mechanism is oil: India imports about 85% of its crude, so every Hormuz flare-up is a tax on its current account and the rupee. Trump's refusal to rule out new Iran strikes before the midterms also knocked Bitcoin (~$84.7k) and Nasdaq futures (CoinDesk). This is an update to the 09-24 India markets story: the new development is the seventh straight weekly decline.

stories.label: KP govt plans deduction from payments made to hospitals under health insurance scheme
stories.summary: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government plans to claw back part of what it pays public hospitals under its free health insurance programme (Sehat Card). This is the PTI flagship that made universal coverage a political brand. Lead with who pays: public hospitals serving the poor lose revenue, and patients may face the shortfall. The structural why is a fiscally stretched province trimming its signature welfare scheme. Explain how the reimbursement flow works and what hospitals say.

stories.label: What the smell of a soil can tell us about soil health
stories.summary: Ecologist Rosa Boone found that soil's smell, which comes from the volatile compounds made by its fungi and bacteria, can be captured and analysed in a lab to read the microbial community. That opens the way to an 'electronic nose' sensor for field monitoring. Lead with the finding: the old farmer's sniff test has a measurable basis. The why is that EU soil-monitoring rules are coming, and DNA sequencing is too slow and costly to scale. For smallholders, a cheap sensor matters more than a lab. This is a real finding; science is under its floor this cycle.

stories.label: Trump expects 'more talks' with Iran soon -- RT World News
stories.summary: New since yesterday's roadmap rejection: explosions were reported near Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz hours after Trump turned down Iran's proposal to reopen it, and the WSJ reports Washington now wants nuclear concessions before talks can resume. Trump says he expects 'more talks', but a source close to Iran's UN delegation told IRNA there are no plans to negotiate in New York. CENTCOM also denies that the IRGC captured its underwater drone. Lead with the blasts and the widening gap between the two sides. Include Ghalibaf's argument that shipping and insurance prices show who controls the strait, and attribute it to him. Attribute the Qeshm blasts to Iranian media.

stories.label: Türkiye slams storming of Al-Aqsa Mosque by Israeli extremist groups
stories.summary: Israeli settler groups again entered the Al-Aqsa compound under police protection, six days after Ben-Gvir led an incursion on 09-21. The repeated entries are wearing down the status quo that bars non-Muslim worship at the site, and Ankara says the Netanyahu government is using them to inflame the region. The only source is TRT World, which is Turkish state media. Attribute the claims to it and to Türkiye's foreign ministry, and do not state the details of the incursion as fact. No independent outlet in the feed covers this event.

stories.label: Serbia's Longtime President Aleksandar Vucic Resigns Post
stories.summary: Aleksandar Vucic, one of Europe's longest-serving leaders, resigned as Serbia's president so that he can run for prime minister in next month's elections. The resignation keeps him in power rather than ending his rule. Lead with the mechanism: by changing office he stays at the top without facing the presidential term limit. Datelined Belgrade.

stories.label: Severe floods across India claim 18 lives, displace thousands amid heavy monsoon rains
stories.summary: Late-monsoon downpours over 48 hours killed at least 18 people across Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Odisha and Chhattisgarh, forced thousands from their homes and damaged crops shortly before harvest. The IMD has issued heavy-rain alerts for 23 states. Lead with the toll and with how late in the season the rains came. Filed as politics, as a disaster story, not as science. Datelined Lucknow.

stories.label: Russia ready to supply India with as much oil as it needs -- ambassador
stories.summary: With Hormuz traffic choked, Russia's ambassador in New Delhi offered to supply India with 'as much oil as it needs'. In the same interview he said Moscow is open to Indian proposals on ending the Ukraine war. The pairing matters: Russia is using India's Gulf supply shock to tie it more closely on both energy and diplomacy. The only source is TASS, Russian state media. Attribute everything to the ambassador through TASS. Datelined New Delhi.

stories.label: UnitedHealthcare Is Dropping Prior Authorization for Roughly 1,700 Medical Procedures in October. Only About 120 Apply to Medicare Advantage, Where It Denied 17% of Standard Requests - AOL
stories.summary: The largest US health insurer is advertising the removal of prior authorization for about 1,700 procedure codes from October 1. Only about 120 of those codes apply to Medicare Advantage, the plan type where it denied 17% of standard requests. Lead with the gap between the headline number and the coverage that actually changes. It is a case study of how an insurer's gatekeeping stays in place behind a PR concession. Datelined Minnetonka.

stories.label: Dario Amodei of Anthropic to Dine With Trump at White House
stories.summary: Trump is hosting Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei at the White House tonight, two weeks after Amodei's call for an AI slowdown angered the president. That call has since drawn an antitrust suit against the labs (09-20) and a refusal from Beijing (09-23), and this week OpenAI paused frontier training. Lead with the reversal from anger to a dinner invitation. The question is whether Washington is moving toward a state-brokered slowdown, which would need the antitrust waiver Amodei has asked for.

stories.label: Afghanistan says 28 fighters killed as Islamabad, Kabul trade accusations
stories.summary: Two Muslim neighbours are killing across their shared border on the same day: the Taliban defence ministry says it killed 28 fighters who crossed from Pakistan into Nuristan, while Pakistan says it killed dozens of 'India-backed terrorists' in Balochistan. Lead with the 28 in Nuristan; the mechanism is each capital blaming the other's proxies, which lets both avoid accountability for civilians in the border belt. Name who says what and do not state either side's labels as fact.

stories.label: Strikes kill 6 in Ukraine, 1 in Russia after Moscow rejects German calls to de-escalate
stories.summary: Continues the Lavrov-Wadephul thread with a material development: the first Russia-Germany foreign-minister talks in years ended with Moscow rejecting Berlin's de-escalation call, and within hours strikes killed 6 in Ukraine and 1 in Russia. Russia's defence ministry (TASS, RT — label as state media) says it hit an Omega Telecom data centre in Kyiv and a Nova Poshta depot in Odesa. Lead with the dead; the mechanism is diplomacy at the UN running alongside strikes on civilian-dual-use infrastructure. Dateline Kyiv.

stories.label: If they didn't, then who killed Naqeebullah Mehsud?
stories.summary: An anti-terrorism court has acquitted the final seven police officers accused in the 2018 killing of Naqeebullah Mehsud, the young Pashtun shot in a staged 'encounter' in Karachi under SSP Rao Anwar. Report the acquittal as the news, not the column's voice: eight years on, no one is convicted for a killing the state's own inquiry called extrajudicial. The mechanism is impunity for police encounter killings, the grievance that launched the Pashtun Tahaffuz Movement.

stories.label: Kano govt restricts durbar after former emir Bayero's public appearance
stories.summary: Kano State banned durbar processions in the metropolis after the deposed 15th emir, Aminu Ado-Bayero, made an unexpected public appearance, to head off clashes between supporters of two rival claimants to one throne. Lead with the ban; the mechanism is a traditional Muslim institution turned into a proxy fight between the state government and federal-aligned rivals, with ordinary Kano residents caught between them.

stories.label: Pope Leo urges Church to face failings
stories.summary: On his France trip Pope Leo XIV told bishops to keep confronting clerical sex abuse and, at Lourdes, called assisted dying 'false compassion' as France legislates on end-of-life law. Lead with the two-track message: accountability for the Church's own abuse record, and direct pressure on a secular state's lawmakers. Dateline Lourdes.

stories.label: Are Netas In Power Becoming Arrogant? Parvesh Verma Slap Row, Scindia's Guna Video Raise Questions
stories.summary: Delhi PWD minister Parvesh Verma was filmed appearing to slap a young man who questioned him during a road inspection in Tilak Nagar; AAP is protesting and Rahul Gandhi has tied it to 'vote chori'. Lead with the video and what the young man asked; the accountability question is what happens to citizens who question ministers in person, and whether any consequence follows for the minister.

stories.label: Maharashtra drought list misses dry pockets; experts say revenue circle a better measure
stories.summary: Farmers in Kolhapur and Nashik with stunted crops and empty soybean pods are shut out of drought relief because Maharashtra declares drought by taluka averages, which wash out dry pockets. Lead with the empty pods; the mechanism is the unit of measurement — experts want the smaller revenue circle — deciding who gets compensation, loan relief and power-bill waivers.

stories.label: Nepal avalanche kills at least 2, leaves several missing
stories.summary: An avalanche hit a staging camp near Himlung Himal in Manang, killing at least 2 and leaving about 10 Nepali guides missing before their clients arrived. Lead with who was on the mountain: local guides who carry the risk of a foreign-client expedition industry, fixing routes ahead of paying climbers. Frame as labour and risk in Nepal's mountaineering economy, not as science.

stories.label: Unsealed Briefs in Authors' Case v. Microsoft/OpenAI
stories.summary: Newly unsealed briefs in the Authors Guild's case against OpenAI and Microsoft allege top executives knew that training on mass-pirated book collections was illegal. Lead with what the documents show executives knew and when; the mechanism is that knowledge undercuts a fair-use defence and exposes the companies to wilful-infringement damages. Attribute every claim to the plaintiffs' filings; the Authors Guild is a party.

stories.label: Why does Bill Gates want AI laws? He says self-regulation is not enough
stories.summary: Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates says AI needs laws from Congress, not company promises, days after OpenAI paused frontier training over safety incidents. Lead with the co-founder of OpenAI's largest backer rejecting self-regulation; the mechanism is that voluntary commitments have no enforcement when a lab's incentives run the other way. Do not re-report the OpenAI pause beyond one line of context.

stories.label: ETH news: Ethereum may not be 'just a blockchain' in 2030, Vitalik Buterin says
stories.summary: Vitalik Buterin laid out a 2030 roadmap in which Ethereum becomes a proof-verification layer more than a blockchain, accelerating after the Hegotá upgrade — but only if developers make zero-knowledge proofs cheaper and coordinate parallel client work securely. Lead with the engineering bottleneck, not the vision; name what has to get cheaper and why.

stories.label: Number of unfrozen lakes in Pakistan grows by 65 in less than 2 months: Suparco
stories.summary: Satellite imagery assessed by Suparco shows Pakistan's unfrozen glacial lakes rose from 40 to 105 between July and August. Lead with the jump from 40 to 105; the mechanism is meltwater pooling behind unstable moraine dams, the precondition for glacial lake outburst floods that hit Gilgit-Baltistan and Chitral villages downstream.

stories.label: UK police evacuate homes near air base used by US
stories.summary: Police evacuated homes in Whelford near RAF Fairford and arrested five people after villagers reported suspicious vans overnight. The US Air Force flies strikes on Iran from this base. Lead with the arrests and the bomb-disposal operation. The structural point: Britain's decision to lend Fairford to the Iran war has brought the war's security risk into a Gloucestershire village. Do not speculate about motive beyond what police have said.

stories.label: Israeli minister calls for West Bank war, annexation of Lebanon, Gaza areas
stories.summary: Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called on Sunday for Israel to annex Gaza at least up to the 'yellow line', along with parts of south Lebanon, and for forces to 'go to war' against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank. Lead with his own words. This is a sitting cabinet minister openly stating annexation as policy, with Gaza's ceasefire lines as the template. Name who would be displaced, and note that annexation of occupied territory is barred under international law.

stories.label: RSF drones strike El Gezira fuel depot as both sides report shootdowns
stories.summary: RSF drones hit the Umm Alila fuel depot east of Wad Madani shortly after dawn prayers and set it on fire, while both sides reported shooting down drones elsewhere. Lead with the target. Fuel is what keeps Gezira's pumps, bakeries and hospitals running in a state the army retook, and the RSF's drone war now reaches civilian supply lines far behind the front. Continuing coverage of the war and the siege of Sudan's civilians.

stories.label: Ukrainian military delivers 4 tons of food to occupied Oleshky by drones, according to regional authorities
stories.summary: Civilians trapped in occupied Oleshky, on the Dnipro's left bank, are being fed by drone: about four tons of food dropped at 100 points across the town, according to the Kherson regional administration. Lead with the method. It shows how cut off the front-line town is, since drones are the only way in. Attribute the figures to the Ukrainian authorities. The same night, Russian strikes killed at least four people and hit a data centre in Kyiv.

stories.label: Iran's IRGC Navy captures 2nd US-made Remus 600 UUV in Hormuz
stories.summary: The IRGC Navy says it has captured a second US-made Remus 600 unmanned underwater vehicle in the Strait of Hormuz. Attribute the claim to Iran's state Mehr News Agency, because there is no US confirmation. Lead with the hardware: the Remus 600 is an autonomous mine-hunting and survey vehicle, and a second capture suggests the US is mapping the strait's seabed. Iran's navy is harvesting the robots sent to do that mapping. The capture comes a day after Trump rejected Tehran's truce offer.

stories.label: Burnham refuses to back 'contested' Heathrow third runway
stories.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has declined to back the £49bn Heathrow third runway, calling it 'contested' and a matter for Londoners. That breaks with Rachel Reeves's growth-first enthusiasm. Lead with the size of the project now in doubt. The mechanism: Britain's flagship infrastructure bet is running into a new leader's political base, and investors and airlines have been planning around a runway that may not come.

stories.label: Bank strike tomorrow: Full list of banks facing work disruption; will HDFC Bank, Axis Bank, SBI, PNB & ICICI Bank remain closed?
stories.summary: Indian bank unions start a three-day nationwide strike from September 28 to 30, demanding a five-day working week. SBI, PNB, Bank of India and Central Bank of India have warned customers that branch services will be disrupted. Lead with the scale: public-sector banks that hold most of India's deposits will go dark over quarter-end. The mechanism is a labour dispute that the finance ministry and the RBI have left unresolved.

stories.label: ‘We cannot take it anymore’: Haiti’s informal vendors protest over gang warfare
stories.summary: Since early August, informal street vendors in Port-au-Prince have been protesting because gang warfare has driven them out of the markets they depend on, and they are asking the government for support. Lead with the vendors' own words. The mechanism is that gangs control the markets and roads, so the informal economy most Haitians live on has collapsed. This is a Latin America dateline the site has been missing.

stories.label: How months of work on the crypto Clarity Act all fell apart
stories.summary: The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, the US bill meant to define who regulates crypto, is dead after months of Senate Banking Committee work. Lead with what that leaves behind: no federal market-structure law, so SEC-versus-CFTC jurisdiction and enforcement-by-lawsuit continue, while stablecoins keep growing. Explain the political and policy factors that sank it. Keep it factual and leave out CoinDesk's analysis framing.

stories.label: DNA reveals chemosynthesis genes in bacteria living on coral reef fish gills
stories.summary: Chemosynthetic bacteria were known from worms and molluscs, but this is the first time they have been found on fish: DNA from coral reef fish gills carries chemosynthesis genes. Lead with the surprise that fish carry a microbiome able to make energy from chemicals. Explain why it matters: gill microbes may shape fish metabolism, immunity and health, which bears on reef resilience.

stories.label: Gunmen kill 17 in South Africa bar shooting, 15 wounded: police
stories.summary: Eight gunmen with assault rifles killed 17 and wounded 15 at a bar near Fochville, west of Johannesburg, searching patrons and taking phones before fleeing; a separate Cape Town attack took the weekend toll to 27. Lead with the numbers, then the mechanism: tavern massacres recur because illegal mining gangs and extortion networks operate where policing is thin, and firearm-control reforms remain unenforced. Who bears it: working-class township residents.

stories.label: Patent Ruling: Apple Ordered to Pay $5.7 Billion
stories.summary: A San Diego federal jury found Apple owes haptics firm Taction Technology more than $5.7 billion for infringing two patents in iPhone and Apple Watch vibration hardware — a record patent verdict. Lead with the size, then the mechanism: US juries price damages as a share of device revenue, so a small component patent can reach billions. Apple denies using the technology and will appeal; the question is whether the award survives, as most outsized verdicts are cut on appeal.

stories.label: 'Countries far from conflicts being penalised': Jaishankar invokes PM Modi's remark at UNGA
stories.summary: At the UN General Assembly, India's foreign minister argued that countries far from today's wars — the Iran/Hormuz oil shock and Ukraine — are paying for them in fuel, food and fertiliser prices, positioning India as spokesman for the Global South's cost-of-war grievance. Lead with that claim and the mechanism (energy import bills, shipping disruption); note he also attacked Pakistan as a 'serial practitioner of terrorism', which reads as a tension with the Global-South-unity framing. Dateline New York.

stories.label: UK's Burnham pledges to offer social care reform at next election
stories.summary: Ahead of his first Labour conference as prime minister in Liverpool, Andy Burnham pledged to put a universal, NHS-style social care service — free at the point of use and funded by everybody — into Labour's next manifesto. Lead with the scale of the promise and the unanswered funding question (who pays, and how). Fold in the same weekend's housing announcement: a revived Help to Buy-style 'Your First Home' scheme with 2.5% deposits and up to 20% state equity loans on new builds under £600,000 — critics say such schemes inflate prices. Dateline Liverpool.

stories.label: CJP Demands Immediate Release After Ashutosh Ranka, 41 Volunteers Detained In Assam Before Key Meet
stories.summary: Assam police detained Cockroach Janta Party co-convener Ashutosh Ranka and 41 volunteers in Guwahati before they could hold a supporters' meeting. Lead with the pre-emptive detention of 42 people for planning a meeting — the mechanism is preventive policing used against a new opposition outfit under Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma's government. Name who ordered it, what law was invoked if reported, and whether charges were filed. Dateline Guwahati.

stories.label: SERAP asks CBN to account for allegedly diverted $6.23m, ₦1.63trn
stories.summary: Nigerian rights group SERAP gave the Central Bank governor a deadline to account for ₦1.63 trillion and $6.23 million allegedly diverted, citing audit findings, plus ₦262.86 billion disbursed under the Anchor Borrowers' Programme with no published list of beneficiaries. Lead with the sums against Nigeria's cost-of-living crisis; the mechanism is central-bank development lending run outside budget oversight. Note SERAP's usual next step is a lawsuit if the bank does not respond. Dateline Lagos (or Abuja per the report).

stories.label: Japan moves to tighten rules for foreigners
stories.summary: Japan is tightening rules for foreign residents even as its shrinking, ageing workforce depends on them — throwing the futures of foreign workers and students into doubt. Lead with who is affected (which visa categories, how many residents) and the contradiction: a labour-short economy restricting the labour it imports. Mechanism: domestic political pressure over immigration versus industry demand. Fills the thin East Asia coverage. Dateline Tokyo.

stories.label: Russian-born businessman elected as new world chess chief -- RT World News
stories.summary: Timur Turlov, a Russian-born Kazakh businessman (Freedom Holding), was elected FIDE president by 196 national federations in Samarkand, after Russian predecessor Arkady Dvorkovich resigned under EU pressure. Angle: how sanctions politics reshapes global sports governance, and Central Asia's rise as the broker. State media only — attribute to 'Russian state broadcaster RT reported' and do not state contested claims as fact. Dateline Samarkand.

stories.label: Hamas leader says Israel to campaign off Gaza's 'blood' in election
stories.summary: Hamas's leader says no Israeli election outcome will change conditions for Palestinians, and that candidates will campaign on Gaza's dead. He also says he is ready to sit down with Abbas. Lead with the argument that the occupation and siege continue whoever wins. Explain the mechanism: Israel's election campaign is running while Gaza's reconstruction and its crossings stay under Israeli control. Give the stated opening to Fatah as the concrete new element. Use Dawn and Arab News for the regional framing.

stories.label: Swiss voters to decide fate of centuries-old neutrality
stories.summary: Swiss voters decide today whether to write a strict definition of neutrality into the constitution. A Yes vote would bar cooperation with military alliances unless Switzerland is attacked, and could constrain its adoption of sanctions. Lead with what a Yes vote would lock out: Bern's deepening defence ties with NATO and the EU. The mechanism is that the Swiss People's Party initiative uses direct democracy to override the government's post-2022 shift. Use RT's framing only as the Russian view, attributed as state media.

stories.label: Why Xi Jinping skipped the UN after his Trump summit
stories.summary: A day after Xi's Washington summit with Trump, Xi sent Vice-President Han Zheng to the UN General Assembly instead of going himself. Han gave only mild words on the US war with Iran and did not mention Taiwan. Lead with the contrast between the two: Beijing is choosing bilateral deals with Washington over a public stage, and is muting its criticism of the Iran war while it pitches itself as the Global South's development partner. Tie this to the $30bn tariff cut already covered; this is the diplomatic follow-through. Use the Anadolu and Tempo sources for the view from outside the West.

stories.label: 'Gyanesh Kumar offered to get me a BJP ticket in 2016,' claims former Kerala Chief Secretary G.G. Thomson
stories.summary: New development on the SIR electoral-roll arc: a former Kerala chief secretary alleges that Gyanesh Kumar, now Chief Election Commissioner, offered him a BJP Lok Sabha ticket in 2016. The allegation lands while the Commission runs a roll revision that the opposition calls vote theft. Lead with the accountability question: the official who rules on the neutrality of the rolls is accused of partisan ties. Fold in the Commission's own moves this week, which are its transparency note on 'unmapped' voters and Delhi's final roll slipping for a fourth time, to 4 December. Attribute the allegation clearly; Kumar's response is needed.

stories.label: Saudi Arabia Rejects Misuse of Vital Maritime Routes
stories.summary: Two moves on the Hormuz toll regime. Riyadh demanded that navigation through Hormuz, Bab al-Mandab and the Red Sea return to pre-28 February conditions, with no fees or restrictions. Iran's new Persian Gulf Strait authority (PGSA) says it will blacklist charterers that route ships off its approved lanes. Lead with the blacklist: Tehran is enforcing its control of the strait through commercial pressure on charterers rather than force. The PGSA warning is reported only by Iranian state news agency Mehr and must be attributed as such. This follows Trump's rejection of Iran's seven-day roadmap.

stories.label: OpenAI pauses training of advanced AI models over safety concerns -- Axios
stories.summary: According to TASS, citing Axios, OpenAI has suspended training of its most advanced models while it and Anthropic investigate tens of thousands of incidents from recent testing and deployment. If this holds, it is the first frontier-lab training pause on safety grounds. Lead with the incident count and the pause itself. The only source in the feed is Russian state news agency TASS relaying Axios: attribute it that way, do not state the pause as fact, and look for Axios or OpenAI's own statement in the fetch.

stories.label: Trump says he is rolling back Biden-era US fuel economy rules for cars
stories.summary: Trump announced new fuel economy standards that undo Biden's rules. The stated aim is cheaper cars and more US production. Lead with the timing: Washington is loosening fuel efficiency in the middle of an oil shock caused by its own Iran war and the Hormuz disruption. Explain who pays: US drivers, through higher fuel demand at wartime prices, and EV investment, through weaker compliance incentives. This is the only US-datelined pick this cycle.

stories.label: African malaria coalition warns 30% funding cut could cause 146m additional cases by 2030
stories.summary: The African Leaders Malaria Alliance projects that a 30% cut in malaria financing would cause 146 million extra cases by 2030. Lead with that number, and with who bears it: African children, above all in Nigeria, which carries the largest share of the world's malaria burden. Explain the mechanism: donor retrenchment is pushing costs onto African treasuries that are already squeezed by the oil shock. Include the leaders' call for domestic financing and the gap between that call and budget reality.

stories.label: United Naga Council seeks Manipur deputy CM Nemcha Kipgen's removal amid fresh violence
stories.summary: Two people were killed in fresh Naga–Kuki violence in Manipur. At tripartite talks with the Centre, the United Naga Council demanded the removal of Deputy CM Nemcha Kipgen, the arrest of her husband, and suspension of the Suspension of Operations pact with Kuki armed groups. Lead with the deaths. Explain the structural issue: New Delhi's ceasefire pact with one armed community is now the grievance of another, three years into Manipur's ethnic conflict.

stories.label: Why AI has trouble predicting the fury of hurricane intensity
stories.summary: AI weather models now rival physics-based forecasts on storm tracks, but they still miss rapid intensification. That is how a storm like Hurricane Polo reaches Category 5 with little warning. Lead with that gap and its mechanism: models trained on historical reanalysis smooth out the rare extremes that matter most. This is the only real science item in the feed. The pick is thin, so the fetch must supply the study details.
